memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If any of your fellow Israelites become poor and are unable to support
themselves among you, help them as you would a foreigner and stranger, so
they can continue to live among you'" - Lev 25:35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When a neighbour began to sink into poverty, God's command was clear:
help them. And the goal was specific — so they could continue to live
among you. The purpose of the help was not merely charity but restoration,
keeping the person within the community rather than letting them slip away.

Notice the timing. God says to help when they are becoming poor — as they
start to slip, not only after they have hit rock bottom. It is far easier to
steady someone before they fall than to rescue them after a total collapse.

Dear reader, there is real wisdom here. We often wait until a person's
crisis is undeniable before we act. God's instinct is earlier — to catch
the person on the way down. A word of encouragement, a timely bit of help, a
listening ear at the right moment can prevent a much deeper fall.

Paul writes, carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the
law of Christ (Gal 6:2). John asks how the love of God can be in someone who
sees a brother in need and has no pity (1 John 3:17).

The aim, always, is that the person can keep standing among us — not
pushed out, not left behind, but held up until they can walk again.

Who around you is beginning to slip? Steady them now.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who in my life is beginning to struggle right now?
2. Do I tend to wait until a crisis before I help?
3. What timely help could prevent someone's deeper fall?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, make me quick to notice those beginning to struggle. Give me
generosity and courage to steady them before they fall. Amen.
